premises.text: Traditional job boards inundate employers with spam and irrelevant applications
premises.evidence_span: out of those 300, 290 are a complete waste of time. Some are spam

premises.text: Qualified job seekers struggle to get noticed and want view and employer feedback
premises.evidence_span: how does my resume or cover letter, the one that's spot on, the one that's perfect for the job I applied to, get noticed?

premises.text: Site posts only handpicked full-time quality jobs without scams or MLM
premises.evidence_span: This is quality jobs for our quality candidates

premises.text: Paid applications signal seriousness so employers notice candidates
premises.evidence_span: job seekers pay to apply on LocalBacon. And they notice that

premises.text: Employers commit to application-view notice and feedback to seekers
premises.evidence_span: agree to give feedback and allow the job seeker to know when they view their application

premises.text: Seekers buy discounted job credits starting at $0.99 to apply and unlock add-ons
premises.evidence_span: The more job credits you buy, the more of a discount we're going to give you. Job credits also allow us to add on other services

premises.text: Flagging syncs to employer ATS; shelving notifies the candidate without changing recruiter habits
premises.evidence_span: if I'm an organization that has an ATS system and I flag a candidate on LocalBacon, that information gets immediately sent to my ATS

domains.name: Employer inbox and seeker notice problems
Credits pricing and ATS employer workflow

value.text: Solve fundamental hiring problems for seekers and employers
value.evidence_span: fix the fundamental problems that exist for both job seekers and employers

causal_links.evidence_span: Monster, CareerBuilder, and Craigslist, they're broken
Job seekers want to get noticed
I gain credibility for giving transparency to my process without changing my behavior

notes: Partition is need / product / commercial-ops; justified because credits+ATS workflow can be revised without changing handpicked listing rules, and the two-sided pain is a separately stated market condition. UI demo features folded into product claims per §4.1(5).
